items.title: catalog_lock: O_EXCL lock file with write and lease modes
items.action: Create harness_lib/catalog_lock.py (standard library only, generic: names no catalog). Constants WAIT_SECONDS=10.0, WRITE_STALE_SECONDS=60.0, LEASE_STALE_SECONDS=1800.0. LockError(RuntimeError). Body JSON {pid, host (socket.gethostname()), owner, mode 'write'|'lease', acquired (time.time()), token (lease only, secrets.token_hex(8))}. hold(path, owner, lease=None, wait=None) is a contextmanager: with lease set, the file must hold a lease whose token matches (else LockError naming 'no lease' or 'token', at once, no wait) and the body runs without touching the file; without lease, create the file with os.open(O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_WRONLY), retrying with random jitter (20-120 ms) until wait (None reads the module's WAIT_SECONDS at call time, so a test can patch it) runs out, breaking a stale holder first; on timeout raise LockError naming the holder's owner, mode and age. The write lock file is removed in a finally. acquire_lease(path, owner, wait=None) -> token (same create/retry/stale rules; a second lease waits and refuses naming the first). release_lease(path, token) removes it; a wrong token raises LockError naming 'token'. break_lock(path) -> Optional[dict] removes any lock and returns its body. read_holder(path) -> Optional[dict] (unreadable body counts as stale-write after WRITE_STALE_SECONDS by mtime). Staleness: write = age > WRITE_STALE_SECONDS, or same host and not pid_alive(pid); lease = age > LEASE_STALE_SECONDS only. pid_alive(pid): POSIX os.kill(pid, 0) (ProcessLookupError False, PermissionError True); Windows ctypes kernel32 OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION=0x1000) + GetExitCodeProcess == STILL_ACTIVE(259), CloseHandle; never os.kill on Windows. Breaking a stale lock: os.replace the file to a unique sibling name then unlink it, so two breakers never both remove a fresh lock. Functions under 50 lines. Copy the planned test file first.

items.title: todo_sync inbox: put one file per item, drain in one locked write
items.action: Create todo_sync/inbox.py. inbox_dir(cfg) = cfg.path(cfg.todo_inbox()). put(cfg, spec, file_issues=False, rng=None) -> PutResult(paths, filed): read_spec(spec, 'items'); load_catalog(cfg, 'add') and validate with add_items on that data (D1 full dry run; with file_issues and items lacking 'issue' use reshape._preview_add) so a refusal raises TodoSyncError and writes nothing; then, with file_issues, reshape._file_pending files the issues; then write each item as {'items': [item]} with report.write_atomic to <inbox>/<UTC %Y%m%dT%H%M%S%fZ>-<secrets.token_hex(3)>.json, returning the paths in spec order. drain(cfg, today=None, rng=None) -> DrainResult(added: ((id, issue|None), ...), rejected: ((name, reason), ...), drift: Optional[int]): list *.json not starting with '.' and not ending .rejected.json, sorted by name (oldest first); none -> empty result. load_catalog once; for each file read_spec + add_items on the working catalog, keeping the result on success and recording (name, reason) on TodoSyncError/RankingError/ValueError. Any accepted: write_edits(cfg, dump_like(working, raw)) (D2 write first), render_snapshot(cfg, today) when todo.snapshots.dir is set, report = check(cfg), write_report(report, report_path(cfg)), drift = report.drift; then unlink the accepted files. Each rejected file: rename to <stem>.rejected.json and write <stem>.reason.txt. The caller holds the lock; drain takes none. drain_lines(result) -> one line: 'inbox: empty', or 'inbox: added N item(s): <id> (#N|note), ...[; rejected M (<names>)]; check drift=<d>' (no check part when nothing landed; 'inbox: rejected M (...)' then). Functions under 50 lines. Copy the planned test file first.

items.title: todo_sync.py: lock every catalog write, lease and inbox subcommands
items.action: Create todo_sync/locking.py: lock_path(cfg) = cfg.path(state_dir)/'locks'/<posix catalog rel with '/' replaced by '__'>.lock; guard(cfg, owner, lease=None) wraps catalog_lock.hold and re-raises LockError as TodoSyncError; acquire(cfg, owner) -> token; release(cfg, token): verify the token (catalog_lock.read_holder), run reshape.apply_refresh(cfg) (recount, Decided 6), render the snapshot when todo.snapshots.dir is set, run check and write the report, then catalog_lock.release_lease; returns the lines to print, the first 'lease released; <refresh head>', the last 'check drift=<d>'; break_(cfg) -> body or None. In scripts/todo_sync.py: add --lease TOKEN to retire, split, refresh and add; add gets --inbox (mutually exclusive with --spec, one of the two required) ; new 'inbox put --spec PATH [--file-issue]' prints one 'queued <repo-relative path>' line per file and 'filed #N <url>' lines; new 'lease acquire --owner TEXT' (prints 'lease: <token>'), 'lease release TOKEN', 'lease break' (prints the removed holder's owner, mode and age, or 'lease: none held'). _dispatch runs every non-dry-run catalog write (add --spec, add --inbox with a file queued (D3), retire, split, refresh, init) inside locking.guard(cfg, '<command line>', args.lease); migrate-ids (non-dry-run) acquires its own lease and releases it in a finally without the recount (Decided 16). Dry runs, check, render, untracked, runner and inbox put take no lock. add --inbox prints inbox.drain_lines. Extend the module docstring for each new subcommand and flag. Keep functions under 50 lines (split _dispatch). Copy the planned test file first.

items.title: todo-watch mod: drain the inbox when a todo-editor agent returns
items.action: config.ts: export DEFAULT_SCRATCH_FOLDER = 'docs/_scratch/' and read scratch_folder into scratchFolder (cleanPath); inboxDirOf(c) = `${scratchFolder}/todo-inbox`. New hooks/inbox.ts: single-flight drain like checks.ts runCycle/requestCheck (one in flight, at most one owed rerun); a drain runs [runner.python, runner.script, 'add', '--inbox', '--project', runner.project] with timeoutMs DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000 through $.process.run and keeps the stdout line starting 'inbox: ' (not 'inbox: empty') as the pending summary; then requests a check refresh. Triggers (spec Decided 17): (a) on('tool.call', { tool: 'Agent' }) for subagent_type 'harness:todo-editor': after next(e), a result with status 'completed' drains now and appends the summary to the result's context; status 'async_launched' records its agentId; (b) checks.ts's turn.complete hook, for an e.agentId recorded in (a), starts the drain (it returns early for subagent loops today); (c) registerContext's prompt.submit adds the pending summary line (awaiting an in-flight drain up to DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS when e.origin.kind is 'task-notification'), then clears it once attached; (d) the session.start hook in register.ts drains when the inbox folder lists a *.json that is not *.rejected.json. The engine allows one session.start and one unmatched turn.complete hook, so (b) and (d) join the existing hooks. New inbox.test.ts covers: foreground return appends context; background return drains on turn.complete and the next task-notification prompt carries the line; two returns while a drain runs give one owed rerun; empty stdout attaches nothing; session start with an empty inbox spawns no process. Add DEFAULT_SCRATCH_FOLDER to the Python mirror test.
